subject: Renewal discussion: proposed upgrade + throughput guarantees for next term
messages:
From: Kate Phillips <kate@glyphsolutions.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — potential capacity bump

Hi Marissa,

Quick note as we start budget planning: our Q3 usage projections show sustained peak inference needs and the team is asking whether we can double our reserved pool at renewal — effectively moving from 8 -> 16 GPUs. The priorities from our side are predictable monthly commit, stronger throughput SLAs for business hours, and a rollout window that won't interrupt our existing pipelines.

Can you share a ballpark for incremental monthly commit and any options for a phased upgrade (e.g., start with 12 GPUs for 30 days before full 16)? Also happy to set up a call with procurement next week.

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Phillips
Director of ML Platforms | Glyph Solutions
procurement@glyphsolutions.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Phillips <kate@glyphsolutions.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — potential capacity bump

Hi Kate — thanks for the heads up and great to hear projection is trending up. High level response below, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan and a quote worksheet for transparency.

Summary (high level):
- Upgrade option: double reserved pool from 8 -> 16 dedicated GPUs for the renewal term.
- Proposed monthly commit delta: 
  - Base (current): 8 GPU-months at existing rate
  - New: +8 GPU-months at list with a renewal discount tier we can offer (see attached).
- Throughput SLO: we can add a 99th percentile per-request latency target for REST calls during 6am–10pm PT with a throughput reservation metric (tokens/minute per GPU pool).
- Phased path: we can provision an interim 12-GPU pool for up to 30 days for validation, with no additional onboarding fee; billing will be pro-rated.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share an updated commitment + discount worksheet (attached).
2) Loop in procurement for contract language; we can add an SLA amendment and a clause for rollback if the phased test shows instability.
3) If that looks good, I’ll send a DocuSign amendment for signatures.

I copied Laura who handles commercial approvals — does procurement need any specific procurement language up front (e.g., PO terms, invoicing cadence)? If you prefer, we can slide into a 30-minute sync with procurement and eng ops this week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: MAP_Glyph_Renewal_v2.pdf (Mutual Action Plan), redwood-dedicated-amendment-quote-8to16.xlsx (quote worksheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-25T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — potential capacity bump (need approval on discount band)

Team — looping you in. Glyph (Kate) is asking to double reserved GPUs at renewal. Their sticker incremental commit is substantial and we have room to offer a renewal-first discount but I need sign-off for the concession and whether we can include a 30-day phased validation period and a 99th pct latency SLO.

Key commercial asks from customer:
- Upgrade 8 -> 16 GPUs for next 12-month term
- Throughput guarantee during 6am–10pm PT (ingress tokens/minute) and 99th pctl latency target
- Option to start at 12 GPUs for a 30-day validation window (pro-rated billing)

Proposed concession:
- 12% renewal discount on the additional 8 GPU-months (applied to incremental commit)
- No fee for the phased 12->16 provisioning
- SLA amendment with credits capped at 1-month invoice (for commercial/legal)

Can you confirm budget approval and whether Legal is comfortable with the SLA cap? If approved, I’ll move to a clean amendment and DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-26T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — potential capacity bump (need approval on discount band)

Marissa — fine to approve the 12% renewal discount on the incremental commit. A couple guardrails:
- Make the price conditioning explicit for a 12-month committed term; do not allow month-to-month at that rate.
- SLA credit cap at one invoice month is ok for a renewal amendment; Legal should validate specific credit terms but commercially good.
- For phased provisioning, require an explicit rollback window and rollback conditions in the MAP (e.g., >10% error increase or >20% latency regression).

Please proceed and route to Laura for contract signature coordination.

-marcus
Chief Revenue Officer (interim)
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Phillips <kate@glyphsolutions.com>, procurement@glyphsolutions.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-03T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Finalized renewal amendment & DocuSign link — 8 -> 16 GPU upgrade

Hi Kate / Procurement team —

Thanks for being flexible. Per our internal approvals, attached is the finalized amendment and the mutual action plan. Highlights:
- Commitment: 12-month renewal; reserved pool increases from 8 -> 16 GPUs (8 incremental GPU-months).
- Pricing: 12% discount applied to the incremental 8 GPU-months for the 12-month term. See spreadsheet for line-item math.
- Phased rollout: optional 30-day validation at 12 GPUs; pro-rated billing for that month. No provisioning fee.
- SLA: 99th percentile latency target for calls during 6am–10pm PT; credit cap = one full invoice month for incidents covered by the SLA.
- Operational: we’ll schedule a short runbook review with your SREs and ours prior to the phased start.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/xyz/sign/GLYPH-2028-RNW-42
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/GLYPH-2028-RNW-42

If you sign by EOD next Friday (2028-05-10) we can lock provisioning for the target renewal start date of 2028-06-01 and meet your Q3 ramp. Let me know if procurement needs payment terms or a PO number included on the invoice.

Best,
Marissa Cole
